properties.name: Type 1 Diabetes
properties.definition: If you have type 1 diabetes, your body makes little or no insulin. Your immune system attacks and destroys the cells in your pancreas that make insulin.

quote: If you have type 1 diabetes, your body makes little or no insulin. Your immune system attacks and destroys the cells in your pancreas that make insulin.

propertyEvidence.insulinRequired: People with type 1 diabetes need to take insulin every day to stay alive.
propertyEvidence.typicalOnset: Type 1 diabetes is usually diagnosed in children and young adults, although it can appear at any age.

properties.name: Type 2 Diabetes
properties.definition: If you have type 2 diabetes, the cells in your body don’t use insulin properly. The pancreas may be making insulin but is not making enough insulin to keep your blood glucose level in the normal range.

quote: If you have type 2 diabetes, the cells in your body don’t use insulin properly. The pancreas may be making insulin but is not making enough insulin to keep your blood glucose level in the normal range.

propertyEvidence.prevalenceShare: About 90% to 95% of diabetes cases are type 2 diabetes.
propertyEvidence.typicalOnset: You can develop type 2 diabetes at any age, even during childhood.

properties.name: Gestational Diabetes
properties.definition: Gestational diabetes is a type of diabetes that develops during pregnancy.

quote: Gestational diabetes is a type of diabetes that develops during pregnancy.

propertyEvidence.typicalOnset: Gestational diabetes is a type of diabetes that develops during pregnancy.
propertyEvidence.prevalenceShare: In 2019, 96 million adults—38% of U.S. adults—had prediabetes.

properties.name: Prediabetes
properties.definition: People with prediabetes have blood glucose levels that are higher than normal but not high enough to be diagnosed with type 2 diabetes.

quote: People with prediabetes have blood glucose levels that are higher than normal but not high enough to be diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. If you have prediabetes, you have a higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes in the future.

propertyEvidence.prevalenceShare: In 2019, 96 million adults—38% of U.S. adults—had prediabetes.
propertyEvidence.predisposesTo: If you have prediabetes, you have a higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes in the future.
